features.name: quest init — Basic Project Initialization
features.description: The `quest init` command accepts a project directory and creates the three scaffold files: init.sh, features.json, and claude-progress.txt
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest init <dir>` creates init.sh in the target directory
Running `quest init <dir>` creates features.json with at least 10 features
Running `quest init <dir>` creates claude-progress.txt with valid JSON
Command exits with code 0 on success
Command prints a confirmation message to stdout when complete

features.name: quest init — --project-name Option
features.description: The `quest init` command accepts a --project-name flag to override the default (directory basename)
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest init <dir> --project-name foo` sets projectName to 'foo' in features.json
Running `quest init <dir> --project-name foo` sets projectName to 'foo' in claude-progress.txt
When --project-name is omitted, projectName defaults to the basename of the target directory
Invalid or empty --project-name prints an error and exits non-zero

features.name: quest init — --description Option
features.description: The `quest init` command accepts a --description flag that is passed to the initializer agent for context-aware feature generation
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest init <dir> --description 'My app'` passes the description to the initializer agent
Features generated reflect the description text when provided
Omitting --description uses an empty string default without errors
The description is visible in the initializer agent's prompt context

features.name: quest init — Nonexistent Directory Error
features.description: The `quest init` command prints a clear error and exits non-zero when the given directory does not exist
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest init /nonexistent/path` prints an error containing the path
The process exits with a non-zero exit code
No partial files are created in the nonexistent directory
Error message is printed to stderr

features.name: quest run — Basic Orchestration Loop
features.description: The `quest run` command starts the full orchestration loop, selecting features one-by-one and invoking coder + evaluator agents
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest run <dir>` begins processing features from features.json
Each feature is processed in priority order (high → medium → low)
The loop stops when all features pass or limits are reached
Progress is persisted to claude-progress.txt after each feature
Command prints per-feature status lines to stdout

features.name: quest run — --max-features Option
features.description: The `quest run` command respects the --max-features flag to limit how many features are processed in one session
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest run --max-features 5` stops after implementing at most 5 features
The count applies to features processed (attempted), not just passed
claude-progress.txt reflects the actual features processed when stopped
Remaining features are not skipped — they stay pending

features.name: quest run — --retry-limit Option
features.description: The --retry-limit option controls how many times the coder agent retries a feature that fails evaluation
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest run --retry-limit 3` allows up to 3 retry attempts per failing feature
After exceeding retry-limit, the feature is marked failed and skipped for this session
A warning is printed when a feature exhausts its retry budget
The retry count resets when a new feature begins

features.name: quest run — --max-resets Option
features.description: The --max-resets option controls maximum context resets per feature before giving up
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest run --max-resets 3` limits context resets to 3 per feature
Exceeding max-resets causes the feature to be skipped with a warning
The contextResets counter in claude-progress.txt reflects resets accurately
max-resets defaults to 5 when not provided

features.name: quest run — --dry-run Option
features.description: The --dry-run flag prints the planned sequence of features without invoking any agents or making changes
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest run --dry-run` lists the features that would be processed
No agents are spawned when --dry-run is active
No files are modified on disk when --dry-run is active
The output clearly labels itself as a dry run

features.name: quest resume — Resume from Last Progress
features.description: The `quest resume` command reads claude-progress.txt and continues from the last known currentFeatureId
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest resume` reads currentFeatureId from claude-progress.txt
Processing continues from the feature after the last completed one
Already-passing features are skipped without re-running
An error is printed if claude-progress.txt does not exist

features.name: quest status — Feature Progress Summary
features.description: The `quest status` command prints a summary of passing/total features and the next pending feature
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest status` prints N/total features with a percentage
The next pending high-priority feature is highlighted
Current feature (if any) is displayed
Command exits 0 even when no features pass yet

features.name: quest status — --show-all Option
features.description: The --show-all flag on `quest status` lists every feature with its pass/fail state
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest status --show-all` lists every feature by id
Passing features are marked with ✓ (or equivalent symbol)
Failing features are marked with ○ (or equivalent symbol)
Priority is shown for each feature

features.name: quest eval — Evaluate a Single Feature
features.description: The `quest eval <feature-id>` command runs only the evaluator agent for one feature and prints detailed results
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest eval <id>` invokes the evaluator agent for that feature ID
Verdict (PASS/FAIL) is printed clearly to stdout
Each acceptance criterion result is printed with a pass/fail indicator
Evidence for each criterion is shown in the output
Command exits non-zero when verdict is FAIL

features.name: quest eval — Missing Feature ID Error
features.description: The `quest eval` command prints a clear error when the given feature ID does not exist in features.json
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest eval nonexistent-id` prints an error mentioning the missing ID
The process exits with a non-zero exit code
The error is actionable (suggests running `quest status` to see valid IDs)

features.name: quest feature — Implement Single Feature Without Evaluation
features.description: The `quest feature <feature-id>` command runs only the coder agent for one feature without evaluating
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest feature <id>` writes a sprint contract and invokes the coder agent
The evaluator is NOT run after the coder completes
Duration and token stats are printed after completion
A warning note is shown reminding the user to run `quest eval` to verify

features.name: quest monitor — Live TUI Dashboard
features.description: The `quest monitor` command launches an Ink/React TUI that streams agent activity from quest-events.jsonl
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest monitor` renders a terminal UI without crashing
The TUI displays historical events from quest-events.jsonl
New events appended to quest-events.jsonl are reflected in the display
The monitor polls for updates at ~500ms intervals

features.name: quest monitor — Nonexistent Directory Error
features.description: The `quest monitor` command prints an error and exits when the given directory does not exist
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest monitor /bad/dir` prints an error with the path
Process exits non-zero
No TUI is rendered before the error

features.name: Orchestrator — Priority-Based Feature Selection
features.description: The orchestrator selects the next feature to implement by ordering: high priority first, then medium, then low; within a tier sorted by array order
acceptanceCriteria: High-priority features are always processed before medium or low
Medium-priority features are processed before low when all high are done
Within the same priority tier, features are processed in their array order
Already-passing features are never selected as next

features.name: Orchestrator — Progress Persistence After Each Feature
features.description: After each feature is evaluated, the orchestrator updates claude-progress.txt with the latest state
acceptanceCriteria: claude-progress.txt is updated after every feature evaluation (pass or fail)
passedFeatures count is incremented when a feature passes
currentFeatureId reflects the feature just processed
lastUpdated is set to the current ISO timestamp
lastCommitSha is updated after a successful git commit

features.name: Orchestrator — Context Reset Detection and Recovery
features.description: When the coder agent requests a context reset, the orchestrator increments the reset counter and retries the feature with a fresh agent session
acceptanceCriteria: A context reset signal from the coder increments contextResets in progress
The orchestrator retries the same feature after a reset
The feature is abandoned when maxContextResets is exceeded
An event is emitted to quest-events.jsonl on each context reset

features.name: Orchestrator — Git Commit After Feature Passes
features.description: When a feature passes evaluation, the orchestrator commits the changes to git and stores the SHA in progress
acceptanceCriteria: A git commit is created after each feature passes evaluation
The commit message includes the feature ID
The lastCommitSha in claude-progress.txt is updated to the new SHA
Commit failure is handled gracefully (warning printed, loop continues)

features.name: Orchestrator — Loop Termination When All Features Pass
features.description: The orchestrator terminates cleanly when all features in features.json have passes:true
acceptanceCriteria: The orchestration loop exits when no pending features remain
A success message is printed showing the total features completed
The process exits with code 0
A final summary event is emitted to quest-events.jsonl

features.name: Orchestrator — Event Emission to quest-events.jsonl
features.description: The orchestrator emits structured JSONL events for all major state transitions to quest-events.jsonl
acceptanceCriteria: Events are appended (not overwritten) to quest-events.jsonl
Each event is valid JSON on a single line
Events include at minimum: type, timestamp, and relevant payload fields
Feature-start, feature-pass, feature-fail, and context-reset events are all emitted

features.name: Coder Agent — Sprint Contract Consumption
features.description: The coder agent reads the sprint-contract.json file to understand what feature to implement before beginning work
acceptanceCriteria: The coder agent reads sprint-contract.json at startup
The feature description from the contract is incorporated into the agent's system prompt
Acceptance criteria from the contract guide the agent's implementation plan
The agent fails fast if sprint-contract.json is missing or malformed

features.name: Coder Agent — File Editing Capabilities
features.description: The coder agent can read, write, and edit source files to implement the target feature
acceptanceCriteria: The coder agent can read existing TypeScript source files
The coder agent can create new files when needed
The coder agent can modify existing files using Edit or Write tools
File changes are reflected on disk after the agent session completes

features.name: Coder Agent — TypeScript Build Verification
features.description: After making changes, the coder agent verifies the build passes by running `npm run build` or `tsc --noEmit`
acceptanceCriteria: The coder agent runs a build check after implementing changes
TypeScript compile errors are detected and the agent attempts to fix them
The agent does not declare success if the build fails
Build output is included in the agent's reasoning

features.name: Coder Agent — Token Usage Tracking
features.description: The coder agent session accumulates token usage statistics (input and output) via the ContextManager
acceptanceCriteria: Input tokens are tracked across all turns of the coder agent session
Output tokens are tracked across all turns
ContextManager.getStats() returns accurate totals after the session
Token stats are included in the completion log line

features.name: Coder Agent — Context Reset Signal
features.description: When the coder agent determines it has lost context or is spinning, it emits a context-reset signal that the orchestrator can detect
acceptanceCriteria: The coder agent can signal a context reset by returning a specific result flag
The orchestrator receives and acts on the context-reset signal
The signal includes a reason string explaining why the reset was requested
The agent does not loop infinitely before signaling a reset

features.name: Coder Agent — Duration Tracking
features.description: The coder agent records how many milliseconds elapsed from start to finish of the session
acceptanceCriteria: The coder agent result includes a durationMs field
Duration is measured from agent start to final response
Duration is printed in the quest feature command output
Duration is included in the quest-events.jsonl completion event

features.name: Evaluator Agent — Writes eval-report.json
features.description: The evaluator agent writes an eval-report.json file with a verdict and per-criterion results after evaluating a feature
acceptanceCriteria: eval-report.json is created in the project directory after evaluation
The file contains a 'verdict' field of 'pass' or 'fail'
The file contains a 'criteriaResults' array with one entry per acceptance criterion
Each entry has 'criterion', 'result' (pass/fail), and 'evidence' fields
The file is valid JSON

features.name: Evaluator Agent — Pass Verdict on Passing Feature
features.description: The evaluator agent sets verdict:pass when all acceptance criteria are satisfied
acceptanceCriteria: When all criteria pass, verdict is 'pass'
All criteriaResults entries have result:'pass'
The orchestrator marks the feature as passes:true in features.json
A pass event is emitted to quest-events.jsonl

features.name: Evaluator Agent — Fail Verdict on Failing Feature
features.description: The evaluator agent sets verdict:fail when any acceptance criterion is not satisfied
acceptanceCriteria: When any criterion fails, verdict is 'fail'
At least one criteriaResults entry has result:'fail'
The orchestrator does not mark the feature as passes:true
A fail event is emitted to quest-events.jsonl with the failing criteria

features.name: Evaluator Agent — Source Code Inspection
features.description: The evaluator agent reads source files to verify implementation correctness against acceptance criteria
acceptanceCriteria: The evaluator reads relevant TypeScript source files before rendering a verdict
Source code evidence is referenced in the 'evidence' field of each criterion result
The evaluator can access any file in the project directory
The evaluator does not modify source files

features.name: Evaluator Agent — Bash Command Execution for Verification
features.description: The evaluator agent can run bash commands (e.g., build checks, test runs) to gather objective evidence
acceptanceCriteria: The evaluator can run `npm run build` and inspect output
The evaluator can run `node` or `tsx` scripts for quick checks
Command output is used as evidence in criteriaResults
The evaluator does not run destructive commands (rm -rf, git reset, etc.)

features.name: Sprint Contract — Generation from Feature
features.description: buildSprintContract() converts a Feature object into a structured sprint-contract.json that the coder agent reads
acceptanceCriteria: buildSprintContract() returns an object with featureId, name, description, and acceptanceCriteria
All acceptance criteria from the Feature are included in the contract
The contract includes a generatedAt timestamp
The contract includes category and priority from the feature

features.name: Sprint Contract — File Write
features.description: writeSprintContract() writes the sprint contract to sprint-contract.json in the project directory
acceptanceCriteria: sprint-contract.json is written to the correct project directory
The file contains valid JSON matching the sprint contract schema
Existing sprint-contract.json is overwritten with the new contract
The function awaits the file write before returning

features.name: Sprint Contract — Read Eval Report
features.description: readEvalReport() reads eval-report.json from the project directory and returns a typed object or null if missing
acceptanceCriteria: readEvalReport() returns the parsed eval report when the file exists
readEvalReport() returns null when eval-report.json does not exist
The returned object is typed with verdict, notes, and criteriaResults fields
Invalid JSON causes the function to throw, not return null

features.name: State — readFeaturesFile()
features.description: readFeaturesFile() reads and parses features.json from a project directory, returning a typed FeaturesFile object
acceptanceCriteria: readFeaturesFile() reads features.json from the given project directory
The returned object has projectName, version, generatedAt, and features array
Each feature in the array is fully typed with all required fields
An error is thrown if features.json does not exist or is invalid JSON

features.name: State — writeFeaturesFile()
features.description: writeFeaturesFile() persists an updated FeaturesFile back to features.json atomically
acceptanceCriteria: writeFeaturesFile() writes the file to the correct path in the project directory
The written file is valid, pretty-printed JSON
The write is awaited before the function returns
Existing content is overwritten (not merged)

features.name: State — markFeaturePassing()
features.description: markFeaturePassing() finds the feature by ID in the FeaturesFile and sets its passes field to true
acceptanceCriteria: The correct feature (by ID) has its passes field set to true
All other features are unchanged
If the feature ID is not found, an error is thrown
The updated FeaturesFile is written to disk

features.name: State — getNextFeature()
features.description: getNextFeature() returns the next feature to implement from the sorted list (first non-passing by priority)
acceptanceCriteria: Returns the first non-passing high-priority feature if any exist
Falls back to medium-priority features when no high-priority features remain
Falls back to low-priority features when no medium remain
Returns null/undefined when all features are passing

features.name: State — countPassing()
features.description: countPassing() returns the number of features with passes:true
acceptanceCriteria: Returns 0 when no features pass
Returns the correct count when some features pass
Returns the total count when all features pass
Does not count features with passes:false or missing passes field

features.name: State — readProgress()
features.description: readProgress() reads and parses claude-progress.txt from the project directory
acceptanceCriteria: readProgress() reads claude-progress.txt from the given project directory
The returned object has all required fields: projectName, totalFeatures, passedFeatures, etc.
Returns null or throws a typed error when the file does not exist
Invalid JSON causes an error to be thrown

features.name: State — writeProgress()
features.description: writeProgress() persists the progress object to claude-progress.txt as pretty-printed JSON
acceptanceCriteria: writeProgress() writes to claude-progress.txt in the correct project directory
Output is pretty-printed (2-space indented) JSON
All fields of the Progress object are included
The write is awaited before the function returns

features.name: Context Manager — Token Accumulation
features.description: ContextManager accumulates input and output token counts across all turns of an agent session
acceptanceCriteria: addUsage() increments totalInput and totalOutput correctly
getStats() returns accurate cumulative totals
Multiple addUsage() calls are summed, not replaced
Initial stats are zero before any usage is recorded

features.name: Context Manager — Reset Method
features.description: ContextManager.reset() clears all accumulated token stats and usage history
acceptanceCriteria: After reset(), getStats() returns zero for all fields
After reset(), the turn history is cleared
reset() can be called multiple times without errors
Subsequent addUsage() calls after reset() accumulate from zero

features.name: Context Manager — Turn Limit Detection
features.description: ContextManager detects when the agent is approaching context limits and signals that a reset is needed
acceptanceCriteria: isApproachingLimit() returns true when total tokens exceed a configured threshold
The threshold is configurable at construction time
When the limit is detected, the coder agent can act on it
The limit check considers both input and output tokens

features.name: Context Manager — Per-Session Statistics
features.description: ContextManager provides per-session statistics including turn count, total tokens, and duration
acceptanceCriteria: getStats() returns turnCount reflecting how many agent turns occurred
getStats() returns totalTokens as input + output sum
getStats() returns session duration in milliseconds
Stats can be serialized to a plain object for logging

features.name: Initializer Agent — Feature Generation
features.description: The initializer agent generates 200+ features based on the project description and existing codebase
acceptanceCriteria: The initializer agent produces at least 200 features in features.json
Features span multiple categories: auth, ui, api, data, performance, security, ux
Each feature has a unique id in kebab-case
Each feature has at least 3 specific, testable acceptance criteria
No feature has passes:true initially

features.name: Initializer Agent — init.sh Creation
features.description: The initializer agent creates an appropriate init.sh for the detected project type
acceptanceCriteria: init.sh is created in the target project directory
The script contains the shebang #!/bin/bash
The script installs dependencies appropriate to the project type
The file is made executable (chmod +x)

features.name: Initializer Agent — claude-progress.txt Creation
features.description: The initializer agent creates claude-progress.txt with correct initial values
acceptanceCriteria: claude-progress.txt is created with totalFeatures matching the generated feature count
passedFeatures is set to 0
currentFeatureId is null
lastCommitSha is null
contextResets is 0
lastUpdated is a valid ISO timestamp

features.name: Initializer Agent — Initial Git Commit
features.description: The initializer agent stages and commits all scaffold files to git after creating them
acceptanceCriteria: init.sh, features.json, and claude-progress.txt are staged after creation
A git commit is made with message 'chore: initialize quest harness'
If no git repo exists, one is initialized first
The commit SHA is printed to stdout

features.name: TUI Monitor — App Component Renders Without Crash
features.description: The Ink App component renders in the terminal without throwing errors on startup
acceptanceCriteria: Running `quest monitor` renders at least one frame without crashing
No unhandled promise rejections occur on startup
The component mounts cleanly even when quest-events.jsonl is empty
The component mounts cleanly when quest-events.jsonl does not exist

features.name: TUI Monitor — Event List Display
features.description: The TUI monitor displays a scrollable list of recent agent events from quest-events.jsonl
acceptanceCriteria: Events from quest-events.jsonl are rendered as rows in the TUI
Each row shows the event type and timestamp
The most recent events appear at the bottom
At least 20 events are visible without scrolling on a standard terminal

features.name: TUI Monitor — Live Event Updates
features.description: The TUI monitor polls quest-events.jsonl and updates the display when new events are appended
acceptanceCriteria: New events appended to quest-events.jsonl are displayed within 1 second
The display updates without requiring a keypress or restart
The polling interval is approximately 500ms
Memory does not grow unboundedly with extended live polling

features.name: TUI Monitor — Feature Progress Bar
features.description: The TUI monitor displays a progress bar showing passing/total features alongside a percentage
acceptanceCriteria: A progress bar is visible in the TUI
The bar shows the ratio of passing to total features
The percentage is computed and displayed numerically
The bar updates when new pass events are received

features.name: TUI Monitor — Current Feature Display
features.description: The TUI monitor prominently displays the feature currently being implemented
acceptanceCriteria: The current feature ID is shown in a highlighted section
The feature name or description is shown alongside the ID
The display updates when a new feature begins
A 'No active feature' state is shown when idle

features.name: TUI Monitor — Token Statistics Display
features.description: The TUI monitor shows cumulative token usage (input and output) for the current session
acceptanceCriteria: Input and output token counts are displayed in the TUI
Counts update as new token-usage events arrive
Tokens are displayed in a human-readable format (e.g., 12.3k)
The section is clearly labeled 'Tokens' or equivalent

features.name: TUI Monitor — Quit Key Handler
features.description: The TUI monitor exits cleanly when the user presses 'q' or Ctrl+C
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing 'q' causes the TUI to unmount and the process to exit
Pressing Ctrl+C causes the TUI to exit cleanly
Exit code is 0 on clean quit
No file descriptors or timers are left open after exit

features.name: TUI Monitor — Error State Display
features.description: The TUI monitor displays error information when events contain error payloads or the event file is unreadable
acceptanceCriteria: Error events from quest-events.jsonl are displayed with a red indicator
If the event file becomes unreadable, an error banner is shown
The TUI does not crash when encountering malformed event lines
Error messages are truncated if longer than the terminal width

features.name: Events — JSONL Event Schema Consistency
features.description: All events written to quest-events.jsonl conform to a consistent schema with required fields
acceptanceCriteria: Every event has a 'type' string field
Every event has a 'timestamp' ISO string field
Every event has a 'sessionId' or 'runId' field for grouping
No event lines are malformed or incomplete

features.name: Events — feature-start Event
features.description: A feature-start event is emitted to quest-events.jsonl when the orchestrator begins work on a feature
acceptanceCriteria: feature-start event is emitted before the coder agent runs
Event payload includes featureId, featureName, and attempt number
Event includes timestamp
Event is a single valid JSON line

features.name: Events — feature-pass Event
features.description: A feature-pass event is emitted when the evaluator returns a pass verdict
acceptanceCriteria: feature-pass event is emitted after a successful evaluator run
Event payload includes featureId, durationMs, and tokenStats
Event includes timestamp
Event is a single valid JSON line

features.name: Events — feature-fail Event
features.description: A feature-fail event is emitted when the evaluator returns a fail verdict
acceptanceCriteria: feature-fail event is emitted after a failed evaluator run
Event payload includes featureId, failedCriteria list, and attempt number
Event includes timestamp
Event is a single valid JSON line

features.name: Events — context-reset Event
features.description: A context-reset event is emitted when the orchestrator performs a context reset for a feature
acceptanceCriteria: context-reset event is emitted on each reset
Event payload includes featureId, resetCount, and reason
Event includes timestamp
Event is a single valid JSON line

features.name: Events — agent-tool-call Event
features.description: Agent tool calls (Read, Write, Bash, etc.) are emitted as events to quest-events.jsonl for TUI visibility
acceptanceCriteria: Each tool call by the coder or evaluator agent emits an agent-tool-call event
Event payload includes tool name and a truncated input summary
Tool call result (success/error) is included in the event
High-frequency tools (Bash, Read) are not suppressed from the event stream

features.name: Events — session-start Event
features.description: A session-start event is emitted when the orchestrator loop begins
acceptanceCriteria: session-start event is emitted at the beginning of `quest run`
Event includes a unique sessionId
Event includes total pending feature count
Event is emitted before any feature-start events

features.name: Events — session-end Event
features.description: A session-end event is emitted when the orchestrator loop terminates (success or limit reached)
acceptanceCriteria: session-end event is emitted when the loop exits for any reason
Event includes reason: 'all-complete' | 'max-features' | 'error'
Event includes total features passed in this session
Event includes session duration in milliseconds

features.name: Logger — Structured Output
features.description: The logger module produces structured, colored terminal output with consistent prefixes for different log levels
acceptanceCriteria: INFO logs are printed with a neutral color prefix
WARN logs are printed with a yellow prefix
ERROR logs are printed with a red prefix
DEBUG logs are only printed when DEBUG env var is set

features.name: Logger — Timestamps
features.description: The logger optionally includes timestamps in log output, controlled by an env var or config flag
acceptanceCriteria: When QUEST_LOG_TIMESTAMPS=1 is set, timestamps appear in log output
Timestamps are formatted as HH:MM:SS
Timestamps appear before the log level prefix
When env var is not set, timestamps are omitted

features.name: Logger — File Output
features.description: The logger can write output to a log file in addition to stdout, configurable via QUEST_LOG_FILE env var
acceptanceCriteria: When QUEST_LOG_FILE=/path/to/file is set, logs are written to that file
Log file entries do not include ANSI color codes
File is opened in append mode
File output does not suppress stdout output

features.name: Security — API Key Not Logged
features.description: The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable is never printed to stdout, stderr, or any log file
acceptanceCriteria: The API key value does not appear in quest-events.jsonl
The API key value does not appear in stdout during normal operation
The API key value does not appear in error messages
Agent system prompts do not include the literal API key value

features.name: Security — Sprint Contract Contains No Secrets
features.description: The sprint-contract.json file written to disk does not contain any sensitive data like API keys or tokens
acceptanceCriteria: sprint-contract.json does not include environment variable values
sprint-contract.json only contains feature metadata from features.json
The file can be safely committed to a public git repository
No secrets are embedded in the agent's initial prompt via the contract

features.name: Security — Path Traversal Prevention
features.description: The CLI resolves all user-provided paths safely, preventing path traversal attacks (e.g., `../../etc/passwd`)
acceptanceCriteria: All user-provided directory arguments are resolved to absolute paths using path.resolve()
The resolved path is validated to ensure it exists before use
Relative paths with `..` components are resolved correctly without special-casing
An error is shown when the resolved path is outside expected bounds (if applicable)

features.name: Security — Evaluator Agent Does Not Modify Source
features.description: The evaluator agent's tool access is restricted so it cannot write or delete source files
acceptanceCriteria: The evaluator agent system prompt explicitly forbids writing or deleting files
The evaluator agent's tool list does not include Write or Edit tools
If the evaluator attempts to call Write, it is rejected with an error
Source files are unchanged after an evaluator run

features.name: Performance — Parallel Criterion Evaluation
features.description: The evaluator agent can evaluate multiple acceptance criteria in parallel rather than sequentially
acceptanceCriteria: Independent criteria checks are issued in parallel when possible
Total evaluation time is shorter than sequential evaluation of the same criteria
All criteria results are correctly collected regardless of order
Token usage is not significantly higher than sequential evaluation

features.name: Performance — TypeScript Build Caching
features.description: The coder agent uses incremental TypeScript compilation to avoid full rebuilds after each file change
acceptanceCriteria: tsconfig.json includes incremental: true or a composite build setup
Subsequent builds after small changes complete faster than full builds
.tsbuildinfo file is created and reused
Cache is not corrupted by agent file writes

features.name: Performance — Event Write Batching
features.description: High-frequency events (e.g., agent-tool-call) are batched before flushing to quest-events.jsonl to reduce I/O overhead
acceptanceCriteria: Events are buffered in memory and flushed in batches
Flush occurs at minimum every 500ms even if batch is small
Flush occurs immediately for high-priority events (feature-pass, feature-fail)
No events are lost if the process is killed

features.name: Performance — Agent Startup Time Under 3 Seconds
features.description: The coder and evaluator agents initialize and make their first API call within 3 seconds of being invoked
acceptanceCriteria: Agent startup (from invocation to first API call) takes less than 3 seconds
Import time for agent modules is measured and logged at DEBUG level
No synchronous file reads block the event loop during startup
The CLI does not preload unused agent modules

features.name: UX — Clear, Actionable Error Messages
features.description: All user-facing error messages include what went wrong and how to fix it
acceptanceCriteria: Missing file errors include the expected file path
Invalid JSON errors include the file path and a hint to validate with `jq`
API errors include the HTTP status code and a link to Anthropic status page
All errors are printed to stderr, not stdout

features.name: UX — Live Progress Bar During Orchestration
features.description: The `quest run` command displays a live progress bar in the terminal during feature processing
acceptanceCriteria: A progress bar is shown in the terminal while `quest run` is active
The bar updates after each feature completes
The bar shows current/total feature count
The bar renders correctly in 80-column terminals

features.name: UX — Feature Completion Notification
features.description: A clear notification is printed when each feature completes (pass or fail) with key stats
acceptanceCriteria: Pass notification includes feature ID, duration, and token usage
Fail notification includes feature ID and the first failing criterion
Pass is shown in green, fail in red
